newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index hits new high of 315.42.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index hits new high of 315.42.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, rose 0.3 percent to a new high of 315.42 at the start of play on Monday.
Latin America edged up 0.8 percent day-on-day to 586.80, Asia was unchanged at 261.18 and Europe, Middle East and Africa were down 0.1 percent at 149.87.
The IFC composite index began 1997 at 294.37, after making gains of 7.0 percent over the course of 1996.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index (BEMI), also denominated in dollars, was up 0.47 percent day-on-day at 171.05 at 0930 GMT.
It began 1997 at 159.57 after rising 8.9 percent over the course of 1996. It touched a high of 171.22 after the end of trading on January 20.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index was up 0.18 percent at 508.415, calculated after the close of trade on Friday.
It began 1997 at 476.315 after making gains of 3.9 percent over 1996. It reached a 1997 high of 508.674 on January 20.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns without dividends from some 21 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns without dividends from 26 emerging market nations. Changes are reported at 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index ELMI, its returns calculated in dollar terms, also hit a new high, rising 0.09 percent to 126.19 by the start of trade on Monday.
It began 1997 at 124.83 after making gains of 14.86 percent over 1996.
By region, Latin America was up 0.25 percent at 104.90, Asia rose 0.03 to 132.39 and East Europe was up 0.04 at 161.25. --Caroline Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
